answer: Behavioral drift fingerprinting. Each identity’s transaction timing, fee rounding, and counterparty mix form a slow-moving signature; the system flags clusters whose signatures stay correlated across a glacier of quiet periods. Enforced rule: newly linked accounts inherit the cluster’s age, so fresh sybils cannot claim clean history. Attackers must run each identity through costly independent behavioral divergence — deliberate wander in timing and fees — paying roughly hours of manual tuning per account, and any slip collapses the ivory of plausible uniqueness into a merged, aged cluster.
